description: Born-Haber cycle for magnesium oxide on a vertical enthalpy axis. Levels from the bottom on the left: Mg(s) + 1/2 O2(g); Mg(g) + 1/2 O2(g); Mg(g) + O(g); Mg2+(g) + 2e- + O(g); Mg2+(g) + O2-(g). Upward arrows join each level to the next; the step from Mg(g) + O(g) to Mg2+(g) + 2e- + O(g) is labelled X. MgO(s) is the lowest level, to the right. Arrow Z goes down from Mg(s) + 1/2 O2(g) to MgO(s). Arrow Y goes up from MgO(s) to Mg2+(g) + O2-(g).

Enthalpy profile against reaction coordinate. Enthalpy axis marked x, y, z from top to bottom. Reactants plateau at y, the curve peaks at x, then falls to the products plateau at z, with an arrow pointing down to the products.

Enthalpy level diagram: enthalpy H against reaction progress. Reactants plateau at a low level, the curve rises to a peak, then falls to a products plateau that is higher than the reactants but below the peak.

Enthalpy level diagram: enthalpy against time. A plateau labelled enthalpy of reactants, a curve rising to a peak, then a fall to a lower plateau labelled enthalpy of products, which is below the reactants.

Two experiments, each pouring sodium hydroxide into hydrochloric acid in a beaker. Experiment A: 50 cm3 of 1.0 mol dm-3 NaOH(aq) added to 50 cm3 of 1.0 mol dm-3 HCl(aq). Experiment B: 50 cm3 of 1.0 mol dm-3 NaOH(aq) added to 100 cm3 of 1.0 mol dm-3 HCl(aq).
Graph of temperature / degrees C against time / minutes, with no numbers on the axes. The temperature is constant at first, rises to a maximum, then falls smoothly back to about its starting value.
Two beakers, each with a 0.05 g piece of Mg giving off bubbles. Beaker A holds 100 cm3 of 1.0 mol dm-3 HCl(aq). Beaker B holds 200 cm3 of 0.50 mol dm-3 HCl(aq).

Labelled apparatus: a spirit burner containing ethanol, with a flame, sits directly below a beaker of water. A thermometer stands in the water, which is heated from below through the base of the beaker.

Energy against reaction progress for a reaction whose products are lower in energy than its reactants, with horizontal guide lines at each level. Arrow A spans the reactant level down to the product level. Arrow B spans the peak down to the reactant level. Arrow C spans the peak down to the product level. Arrow D spans the product level down to the horizontal axis.

Born-Haber cycle for strontium chloride on a vertical enthalpy axis, values in kJ mol-1. Going up from Sr(s) + Cl2(g): +164 to Sr(g) + Cl2(g); +243 to Sr(g) + 2Cl(g); +550 to Sr+(g) + 2Cl(g); +1064 to Sr2+(g) + 2Cl(g). Then -698 down to Sr2+(g) + 2Cl-(g). SrCl2(s) is the lowest level, reached by -829 down from Sr(s) + Cl2(g). An arrow labelled lattice enthalpy goes up from SrCl2(s) to Sr2+(g) + 2Cl-(g).

Potential energy against reaction coordinate for a catalysed and an uncatalysed reaction, sharing a reactant level and a higher product level, so the reaction is endothermic. The uncatalysed curve has the higher peak. Arrow z spans the reactant level up to the product level. Arrow x spans the product level up to the catalysed peak. Arrow y spans the product level up to the uncatalysed peak. The answer options follow as a table.

Born-Haber cycle for potassium oxide. Going up from 2K(s) + 1/2 O2(g): +428 kJ to 2K(g) + O(g); +838 kJ to 2K+(g) + 2e- + O(g); +612 kJ to 2K+(g) + O2-(g). K2O(s) is the lowest level, reached by -361 kJ down from 2K(s) + 1/2 O2(g). An arrow labelled lattice enthalpy goes up from K2O(s) to 2K+(g) + O2-(g).

Hess's law cycle. Across the top, CaCO3(s) goes to CaO(s) + CO2(g) with enthalpy change deltaH. Each side reacts with 2HCl(aq) and an arrow runs down to the shared product CaCl2(aq) + H2O(l) + CO2(g): deltaH1 from CaCO3(s) and deltaH2 from CaO(s) + CO2(g).

Graph of deltaG / kJ (from -60 to +10) against temperature T / K (from 0 to 700). A straight line with negative gradient runs from about +5 kJ at 300 K, crosses deltaG = 0 at about 330 K, and reaches about -50 kJ at 600 K.

Calorimeter: a beaker of water containing a thermometer and a stirrer, with a coiled metal tube running through the water. A small burner containing ethanol sits below, and its hot gases pass up through the coil.

Hess's law cycle. Step 1, across the top: CH2=CH2(g) + H2(g) to CH3CH3(g). Step 2 runs down from the reactants, with + 7/2 O2(g), to 2CO2(g) + 3H2O(l). Step 3 runs down from CH3CH3(g), with + 7/2 O2(g), to the same products.

Graph of temperature / degrees C (24 to 32) against volume of hydrochloric acid added / cm3 (0 to 50) on graph paper. Points read approximately: 0, 25.0; 5, 25.8; 10, 27.0; 15, 28.0; 20, 28.8; 25, 29.8; 30, 30.1; 35, 30.0; 40, 30.0; 45, 30.0; 50, 29.8. No line is drawn; the student is asked to draw lines.
